fact: The education minister says in a November 2025 interview that the ministry, through its GOSE and SMIS platforms, now has reliable data to detect pupils in difficulty before they drop out, and that more than 3,000 pupils have been supported through the system; he does not say who enters the data, how often, or at which school levels.

The education minister's start-of-year circular of 1 September 2025 makes consolidating the SIGE, through the GOSE and SMIS platforms, a priority strategic axis for 2025-2026, so as to produce regularly updated data, identify pupils at risk and make individual pupil follow-up a key instrument; it is a ministerial circular, not a costed plan.

La Nation reports that the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training itself directs the SIGE and its GOSE and SMIS platforms, through the minister's circular of 1 September 2025 to all staff of the sector.

GPE reports in January 2024 that, under the PRODA project (US$30.35 million from the World Bank, GPE and Education Above All, of which US$11.55 million GPE), a new digital education management platform is gradually being developed, introducing a unique identification number for each student so that progress can be tracked through the school career; no date is given, so the publication date is used, and no schools using it are stated.

GPE states in January 2024 that PRODA, under which the new digital education management platform is being developed, is managed by the education ministry (MENFOP) and is the largest programme it has managed; the publication date is used as no other is given.

The World Bank's September 2019 appraisal gives the baseline for 'Modernization of the EMIS' as No, with a student information system still to be developed as the end target; the project is to introduce unique student identifiers and a student-level tracking system that did not yet exist.

As appraised by the World Bank in September 2019, the student-level tracking system for basic education was planned, not in use at any level: technical assistance was first to assess the existing data collection system and recommend a solution.

The World Bank appraisal of September 2019 finances the modernisation of MENFOP's education management information systems under Component 4, costed at US$2.55 million: US$0.8 million IDA grant and US$1.75 million GPE grant, with no domestic contribution stated for it.

The World Bank appraisal of September 2019 names MENFOP as implementing agency for the EMIS modernisation, with its directorate of planning and statistics and its ICT directorate to be trained on the enhanced systems.

The World Bank's status report says that, as at 28 November 2023, GOSE holds a student-management module covering enrolment, ID number, orientation and absences, gives each pupil a unique identifier, has the school principal register and transfer pupils in the application, and has pupil and teacher absenteeism transmitted to central management through it; student grades and history are options MENFOP plans to add.

The World Bank's status report says that, as at 28 November 2023, each pupil has a unique identifier in GOSE from pre-school to senior school and that all public schools transmit their data through the application.

The World Bank's status report says that, as at 28 November 2023, all public schools transmit their data via the GOSE application, which is being rolled out in phases, and that MENFOP plans to extend it to refugee and private schools; it gives no count of schools and no total, and the indicator whose target is 70% of public and 50% of private primary schools transmitting on time is still recorded as 'No'.
The World Bank's status report says, as at 28 November 2023, that GOSE was developed by MENFOP, the education ministry, which also plans its extension.

The World Bank's status report, as at 28 November 2023, carries 'Modernization of the EMIS' and 'Improved methods for data collection' as results indicators of Component 4 (data systems, US$2.55 million) of a project financed by IDA and trust funds including GPE; it names no domestic budget line for GOSE.
